lines.text: When you stream a video from across the world, it almost never comes from space. It comes along the ocean floor.
Undersea cables carry about ninety nine percent of the data that crosses the oceans.
In deep water, many of these cables are only about an inch thick, lying right on the seabed.
Inside are glass fibers as thin as a hair. Your data rides through them as flashes of laser light.
Light fades over distance, so repeaters along the cable boost it again, often around every hundred kilometers.
They get their power through the cable itself, at up to fifteen thousand volts.
And the biggest danger isn't sharks, even though they've bitten cables. It's fishing boats and ship anchors.
